scenes.title: Born beside the Little Colorado
scenes.assetBrief: Wide observational charcoal of the Little Colorado floodplain, irrigation and a sparse Woodruff-area settlement in 1886. Approved after a 30 percent zoom followed by an additional 15 percent zoom (49.5 percent tighter than the original composition); distant figures are ambiguous and no family likeness is claimed.

scenes.title: Territorial Arizona
scenes.assetBrief: Public-domain National Archives photograph of two Mormon women and their small children outside a building at Mormon Dairy near present-day Mormon Lake, Arizona Territory, 1887–1889. This is northern-Arizona Mormon settlement context from Jonathan's infancy; it is not Woodruff and no Webb family member is depicted.

scenes.title: A marriage in northern Mexico
scenes.assetBrief: Public-domain circa-1900 photograph of Mormon colonists with horses and wagons outside a small store in northern Mexico. It provides regional settlement and clothing context close to Jonathan and Della's 1908 marriage period; the specific colony is unidentified, so it is not represented as Colonia Morelos and no Webb or Ray relative is claimed.

scenes.title: A route left unresolved
scenes.assetBrief: Approved crop from Rand McNally's 1913 United States map in the Atlas of the Mexican Conflict, with project-added endpoint markers for Pinedale, Arizona, and Colonia Morelos, Sonora. The dotted curve is explicitly conceptual: it does not claim an exact road, migration date or immediate cause.
scenes.place: Colonia Morelos, Sonora → Pinedale, Arizona • route and date unresolved
scenes.contextNote: Pancho Villa's documented protection of Mormon colonists in Chihuahua in 1912 is retained as qualified regional context only. No direct connection to Jonathan Webb, Della Ray or Colonia Morelos has been established, and it is not presented as the cause of this family's move.

scenes.title: North to Arizona’s pine country
scenes.assetBrief: Photo-only USDA Forest Service photograph of a mixed forest stand in Apache National Forest in 1910. It establishes period White Mountains forest context near the family's later Pinedale setting; it is not represented as Pinedale itself and no Webb family member is pictured.

scenes.title: A family across the White Mountains
scenes.assetBrief: Portrait-format USGS topographic base with project-added markers for the five places named in the supported family narrative: Pinedale, Lakeside, Vernon, Snowflake and McNary. The markers show geographic context only; no route, sequence or person-specific residence is inferred from their placement.
